thread.title: Trisura: Brookfield's Child Will Grow Stronger - Trisura Group Ltd (OTCMKTS:TRRSF)

author: Aitezaz Khan
title: Trisura: Brookfield's Child Will Grow Stronger - Trisura Group Ltd (OTCMKTS:TRRSF)
text:
Trisura Group ( OTCPK:TRRSF ) is a Canada-based specialty insurance provider that deals in Risk Solutions, Surety, Corporate Insurance and Reinsurance segments and is targeting the geographically dispersed customer base through its three subsidiaries: Trisura Guarantee Insurance Company (Canadian operations), Trisura Specialty Insurance Company (US operations) and Trisura International Insurance Limited (International Operations).
Trisura is listed on TSX (read: Toronto Stock Exchange) since June 2017 and trades with the symbol of "TSU" and also trades in the US 'over-the-counter' as TRRSF. Trisura emerged as a spin-off from Brookfield Asset Management ( BAM ); an asset management giant having a market cap of around US$ 40.87 billion. Although TRRSF has a very low market cap of around US$ 133.5 million (primarily due to the limited ~6.6 MM outstanding shares), however it has the full support of Brookfield and given the fact that TRRSF has significant potential for operational growth (which is discussed later in this article) I believe that an injection of fresh capital through issuance of new shares may witness a future boom in TRRSF's market cap and it may well start trading on a major American stock exchange soon.
BAM's support for Trisura during start-up phase: Before the spin-off, TRRSF was part of BAM's insurance operations and BAM decided to execute this transaction in an attempt to focus on its core operations. Another reason to establish a separate listed entity was to leverage the specialty insurance business with increased availability of capital and to maintain transparency while attaining a sustainable growth rate through diversified operations. TRRSF has experience in managing the Canadian and International operations. However, it is new to the US market and has little experience there.
Source: Trisura website
The US segment is where TRRSF requires the greatest support from BAM and BAM has fulfilled this need by providing executive support (senior officers and directors) to build the business up and get it running. In this context it is relevant to mention that Greg Morrison (CEO/director/president of Trisura) and George Myhall (chair of the Trisura Board) also hold senior positions in BAM.
Additionally, by virtue of the dynamics of spin-off transactions; BAM's Class-A and Class-B shareholders were given one share of TRRSF for every 170 shares held. It is noteworthy that BAM has kept its share in the management of TRRSF's business. For instance, consider the case of Partners Value Investment LP ( OTC:BNBMF ) which has a significant investment in BAM (86 million Class A shares) and was entitled to 0.36 million shares of TRRSF according to the share distribution scheme. However it purchased an additional 0.58 MM shares from TSX to maintain a significant interest of ~16.2% in the newly established company.
In my opinion, this is another factor that indicates the hidden value of this stock because BNBMF only holds interest in high value stocks like Apple ( AAPL ), General Motors ( GM ), Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ), Proctor and Gamble ( PG ), Pfizer Inc. ( PFE ) and Coca-Cola ( KO ). The table below provides the performance of these selected stocks and highlights that these stocks have generate ROA (read: return on assets) up to ~15% over the past twelve months. Another interesting fact about BNBMF's portfolio is that only APPL, BAM and now TRRSF have generated constant returns over the period in picture.
Source: YCharts
Trisura's Specialty Insurance Business Review: To assess how this spin-off transaction has affected Trisura's business let's first consider the company's performance during the first quarter.
The balance sheet for Q1: A review of the balance sheet for Q1 2018 indicates that there was no significant change in the balance sheet figures with the total assets declining slightly from CA$ 488 MM to CA$ 486 MM. This decline was partly offset by a decline in total liabilities from CA$ 367 MM to CA$ 362 MM.
The major loser on the asset side was the cash and cash equivalents; going down from CA$ 166 MM to CA$ 105 MM (down 37% Q/Q) however the investments ( that comprise of fixed income investments, shares and units of mutual funds etc.) increased from CA$ 191 MM to CA$ 248 MM (up 30% Q/Q). In my view, this transfer between assets is a favorable move as cash has been put to productive use.
The income statement for Q1: Let's have a look at the income statement for the Q1 2018:
Source: Trisura Q1 financials (values in CA$ 000's)
By taking a closer look at the group's financial performance for the first quarter on a Y/Y basis, one can see that gross and net premiums increased by 22% and 23% respectively. Since this was TRRSF's first year of operations after spin-off I can foresee voluminous growth in business underwritten during the future years as TRRSF will build on experience and reputation in its new geographical segment (US) through Trisura Specialty Insurance Company.
Since new underwriting business does not come without associated costs so we can identify that total claims and expenses have increased from CA$ 19 MM to CA$ 21.3 MM (up 12% Y/Y). In my view the increase in expenses was not proportional to the increase in premiums and has helped convert a net loss of around CA$ 4 MM to a net income of CA$ 1.8 MM on a Y/Y basis. So far so good; and when we consider the total comprehensive income figure we see a total comprehensive loss of CA$ 3.2 MM being converted into income of CA$ 2.1 MM, again on a Y/Y basis.
I can see other favorable financial metrics for TRRSF; have a look at the following numbers taken from Trisura's Financial Supplement for the Q1:
Source: Trisura financial supplement
Comment-red box: This indicates that around 96% of TRRSF's gross premiums were written from Canadian operations (or may I call it Trisura's fortress). As illustrated earlier Trisura has carried out Canadian insurance operations since 2006 and the 12+ years of experience gives management an edge in this business. Additionally, the infant US operations carried through Trisura Specialty Insurance Company present a great opportunity for growth if the company can deploy a team of experienced professionals to capture a greater market share and sell more insurance policies in the US. However, I believe that this will be the tricky part because TRRSF has to face competition from well-established companies like W.R. Berkeley Corporation ( WRB ), Markel Corporation ( MKL ) and Mercury Insurance Corporation ( MCY ). Although these selected companies specialize in different lines of businesses including P&C, automobile, renters, business insurance and reinsurance etc., but for TRRSF they are a competitor because TRRSF deals in different types of specialty insurance. In my opinion, the only way out for TRRSF to capture a market share in the US, is to compete by pricing its policies lower than the competitors.
Comment-yellow box: This represents the company's premium revenue by segment and is further clarified by the pie chart below:
(Prepared by Aitezaz Khan for Seeking Alpha)
It can be seen from the chart above that the most successful stream of revenue is the Canadian based risk solutions that include warranty programs and fronting solutions. Then again, the US based risk solutions present a great opportunity for growth however the position is threatened by large competition. As shown in the diagram below, Trisura incurred net underwriting loss of around CA$ 0.6 MM during Q1.
Source: Trisura financial supplement
However, I think the company has to incur high administrative costs to establish its roots in the US markets and eventually it will become profitable in the US segment as well.
Comment-blue box: At the time of writing this article, the share price of Trisura is around CA$ 27 however the book value per share is around CA$ 18.68 (up 0.19%) and the share price is gaining momentum since the last month.
Source: Trisura
This gives TRRSF a PB ratio (read: price-to-book) of 1.43 which is lower than that of competitors. If we consider TRRSF's price-to-book with peers it indicates that TRRSF's is undervalued compared with its well-established peers.
Source: TRRSF data by YCharts
If you add the fact that business has grown over the past 12 months (as discussed in a previous section), it is easy to see why there is a lot of upside to this stock.
Last word: To cut a long story short, Trisura has posted improved results over the last 12 months and has opportunities to expand its US operations with the support of BAM's experienced team. Furthermore, as the share is undervalued compared with peers I think this is a good value stock with potential upside.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
